31028,2730,Goal selection for WP,"The goal selection for WP allows users to select goals (with option `-wp-prop`) by name (tagname) of the goal or by type of the goal. On large projects, it can be convenient to select goals also by function name in addition to a selection by a goal name, since the same names of goals appear in several functions. Is it possible to select goals by goal name AND function name? The documentation does not indicate if this is possible. If not, this can be a useful feature.
Today, it can be possible to limit a proof to certain function(s) (with option `-wp-fct`) but it is not convenient for a full proof.

This feature would be particularly useful for strategies to target a certain goal ONLY in a certain function in `@\wp::proof` because very often, a specific goal in a specific function requires a specific proof script.
More generally, targeting more precisely a specific goal, for instance by the full goal name with the function name and tagnames (like in the name of the recorded script) would be very convenient.
The option `-wp-auto-depth` limits both the application of some tactics (like Wp.split) AND application of strategies for children.
It can be illustrated by the attached example [test.c](/uploads/7679238814f2f628643a8cbd8e568503/test.c)

With option `-wp-auto-depth 1` we observe that tactic Wp.split is not applied recursively (as illustrated by RangeThenProver_3 and RangeThenProver_1). But this option also limits explicit application of strategy RangeThenProver_2 while it is specified for children.

With option `-wp-auto-depth 10` we observe that tactic Wp.split is applied recursively (as illustrated by RangeThenProver_3 and RangeThenProver_1). This option also allows explicit application of strategy RangeThenProver_2 for children.

The user may need to apply Wp.split just once and at the same time apply (same or different) strategies several times when this application is specified for children. Systematic application of Split multiple times uselessly increases the number of goals and proof time.

It would be preferable to let the user to control the depth of application: if the user needs to apply Wp.split or any other tactic or strategy recursively or a certain number of times, they specify it explicitly for children.
It seems that there should be different options for the maximal depth of application of strategies and the number of forced applications of some tactics like Split, but this should not be the same.
### Termination of recursive application of Split

In the case of application of Split to the condition of an if (as illustrated by strategy SplitBranch in the attached example), the same condition is added into the `when` clause. For that reason, the application is performed recursively again and again as the condition remains present in the `when` clause.
A solution can be to specify a pattern in `if(...) ... else ...` form to target only the condition in the if statement) to avoid useless application of the Split in such cases.

column1: 31800,2777,"GCC machdeps declare __builtin_fmod{,f,l} with one argument","## Summary
In GCC machdeps, the three `__builtin_fmod*` declarations have one parameter instead of two. Correct GCC code therefore fails during parsing.
double f(double a, double b) { return __builtin_fmod(a, b)
[kernel] k_fmod.c:2: User Error: Too many arguments in call to __builtin_fmod

The `fmod`, `fmodf`, and `fmodl` GCC builtins each take two arguments. Change each declaration to have two arguments of the corresponding floating type, and add a parsing regression test. It would also be sensible to audit nearby binary math builtins.

We are actively updating frama-clang, and this is one of the remaining kernel blockers for its C++17 standard-library parse corpus.
